db_evidence.notes: The fact is retrievable but only via an exact-keyword match: episodes:30sec:002371 / episodes:3min:000395 (71100-71160/71280) and semantic_triples:0001146 (71160s, score 0.638 for query '九叶灵芝精') explicitly name '九叶灵芝草种子' and '九叶灵芝精' as loot dropped after defeating a quadruped enemy in this window. No episodes/visual_clips row for this window literally describes 'red mushrooms growing on the body' in text -- that visual fact only surfaces via clip_qa inspecting the actual frames. Meanwhile a separate, unrelated toad-like boss encounter at 53900-54030s has episodes/visual_clips/object_states text explicitly describing a 'green poison-effect marker' and 'spreading green gas cloud', which scores highly (0.5-0.65) against generic 'poisoned body swells/turns green' semantic queries and acts as a strong distractor for any rollout that searches with generic poison-body language instead of the specific enemy name.

root_causes: Distractor collision: a separate toad-like boss fight at ~53900-54030s has DB text explicitly mentioning 'green poison-effect marker' and 'spreading poison gas', which out-competes the correct window in semantic_search when queries use generic phrasing like 'poisoned body swells/turns green' instead of the specific enemy name '九叶灵芝精'.

The correct window's textual evidence in the DB is indirect (a loot-notification line naming the item '九叶灵芝精', not a direct description of 'red mushrooms on body'), so only an exact keyword search (episodes/semantic_triples LIKE '%九叶灵芝%') reliably surfaces it; broader semantic embedding queries drift toward the more visually-explicit distractor.

Two of the three failing rollouts (0) actually located the correct window via a precise semantic_triples hit early on, but then abandoned it after a generic follow-up query returned the distractor with a higher-looking match, i.e. a failure to commit to/re-verify already-found correct evidence rather than a pure retrieval failure.

Rollout 3 additionally misread the wrong clip's visual content (reported black slime vs. the green haze reported by other rollouts on the same distractor window), compounding the wrong-window error with a visual misperception.
what_worked: Rollouts 1 and 4 used precise, entity-name-anchored searches (run_sql LIKE '%九叶灵芝%' UNION across multiple tables, or repeated targeted run_sql) rather than relying on generic descriptive semantic_search queries, which let them converge on the correct 71054-71157s window without being pulled toward the distractor.
Once clip_qa was pointed at the correct window, it reliably and correctly identified the red lingzhi growths, showing the visual sub-agent itself is capable when given the right time range.
transferable_lessons: When a question names a specific enemy/item (e.g. '九叶灵芝精'), keep that exact term in every follow-up search rather than switching to generic descriptive language ('poison', 'body swells', 'turns green') -- generic terms can match unrelated but visually similar encounters elsewhere in the video.

Prefer exact-keyword run_sql (LIKE) searches across all relevant tables in one shot when a named entity is available; this is more precise than iterative semantic_search with paraphrased queries once initial semantic hits are ambiguous.

If a specific-keyword search already returns a strong top hit (e.g. score 0.6+) for the exact entity, treat that as the authoritative window and verify it with clip_qa before exploring further, rather than continuing to search with looser language that can surface higher-scoring but unrelated distractors.

Cross-check clip_qa results against the entity named in the question (does the described scene actually involve that specific enemy/item?) before submitting, since a plausible-looking 'poison' visual in the wrong scene can still be self-consistent and convincing.
